title: Hamlet his father showeth the prince no blister of combustion
html_source:
The ghost of Hamlet’s father says to Hamlet,

But that I am forbid
To tell the secrets of my prison house,
I could a tale unfold whose lightest word
Would harrow up thy soul […]
But this blazon must not be
To ears of flesh and blood.

The inference is not about Hamlet Sr.’s murder; he is telling his son that he is imprisoned in an environment that would act as if to explode in blistering flames, were he allowed to describe it. This description of the reward for decadence, combined with that referred to in the succeeding sentence, referring to Dante’s Inferno, appears to be a warning of dark and dismal Hell. Again, the reader must determine for himself whether this is Joyce’s satire or seriousness.
